A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WAVE forecasting study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; relocated material can be matched without unresolved reading gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments on 12 datasets, including AR/WAVE comparisons, ablations and attention visualizations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds loss/tokenization ablations, a TimesNet comparison and results under multiple random seeds.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.8 retain the tokenization, AR/MA mechanism, indirect weight generation, activation functions and parameter sharing. The new ablation variants do not replace the proposed WAVE procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 forecasting datasets and retain short-horizon, long-horizon and extended-lookback scenarios. New appendix experiments use existing dataset subsets; broader tasks discussed in related work are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 15 adds TimesNet as a comparator on Weather and the four ETT datasets at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720. The previously reported baseline and attention-comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: Tables 13–14 introduce experimental controls without the AR loss and with multivariate tokenization. Previously stated splits, preprocessing, metrics, budgets and lookback settings are retained. Detailed settings connecting the new ablations to existing experiments are not supplied.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct tests of the AR training loss and tokenization choice on ETTm1/ETTm2, plus seed stability on ETTh1. These substantially extend the questions examined beyond the retained depth, lookback, activation-function and attention-visualization analyses.

E5.justification: v2 specifies seed 2024. v4 Table 16 additionally reports individual outcomes for seeds 2024–2028 for standard and linear AR/WAVE models on ETTh1. This is a localized addition; the general settings text still specifies 2024, and no aggregate uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 2–12 retain their numerical results, while Tables 13–16 add ablation, TimesNet and seed outcomes. Some new control entries are inconsistent: ETTm1/12 Std-Attn MSE labeled 'Original' is 0.136 in Table 13 versus 0.218 in retained Table 8. No setting distinction explains this, so it cannot establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds Proposition A.1 and a stepwise proof of O(Nd²) complexity for an efficient linear-attention implementation, explicitly linear in sequence length for fixed dimension. The existing indirect-MA derivation and decay analysis remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims: competitive autoregressive forecasting, efficient incorporation of MA terms, separation of local and longer-term patterns, and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of local/seasonal decoupling, linear versus gated attention, and computational overhead are retained. The inter-series modeling limitation and proposed broader applications also remain; the added experiments receive no substantive interpretive discussion.

D1.justification: The abstract's code hyperlink changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to the named GitHub repository LJC-FVNR/ARMA-Attention. Hardware, hyperparameters, optimization, normalization and data-access instructions otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands the earlier related-work discussion with linear-attention history, broader time-series analysis tasks and forecasting developments. Added references include TimesNet, Seamcarver and literature on anomaly detection, classification, clustering, imputation and change-point detection. The existing positioning against EMA approaches and ARMA cells is retained.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'Varing' to 'Varying', updates publication/header text, regularizes the appendix hierarchy and expands the related-work narrative. Most main-text prose and its argumentative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes full-width, Tables 13–16 are added, and several appendix displays are resized or reordered. Figures 7–8 move ahead of the detailed forecasting tables. Existing plot content is retained rather than replaced by new visual analyses.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful evidence beyond v2's single-seed reporting, particularly the five-seed ETTh1 comparison, and supplies explicit complexity accounting and additional experimental checks. The gain is limited by poorly documented new ablations, inconsistent 'Original' entries in Tables 13–14, and proof notation not reconciled with the main residual definition. The central benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
